levels.title: Office Orientation
levels.blurb: First day at NovaCorp. Meet the team and spot baiting, QR traps, exposed passwords and unlocked screens.
intro: Welcome to NovaCorp. It's your first day.
Gold markers show where you're needed. If a goal is off-screen, follow the gold arrow at the edge.
Start by meeting Ada in the IT & Server Room.

tasks.label: Meet Ada in IT
talk: Ah, the new intern. I'm Ada. I lead IT Security here.
Attackers rarely break through firewalls. They walk in through people.
Four red flags are hidden on this floor. Each one is glowing gold for you today.
Inspect each one, then decide what to do. Come back when you're done.

enc.title: A USB drive on the cafeteria floor

art.desc: A blue USB drive lies under a table. The label reads 'Salary_Revisions_2026'.

inspect.c: 'Salary_Revisions_2026': a label designed to make you curious.
No one nearby is looking for it. It was left where lots of people pass.
No name, no IT asset sticker. Company drives always carry one.

acts.l: Plug it into your laptop to find the owner
acts.fb: That's exactly what baiting relies on. A malicious drive can run code the moment it's connected.

acts.l: Hand it to IT without plugging it in
acts.fb: IT can examine it safely on an isolated machine.

acts.l: Leave it where it is
acts.fb: You didn't plug it in, but the next person might.

acts.l: Drop it at reception's lost and found
acts.fb: Better than plugging it in, but unknown drives should go to IT.

enc.lesson: Never plug in a drive you didn't get from IT. Curiosity is the attack.

enc.title: A free-lunch poster with a QR code

art.desc: A bright poster on the cafeteria wall: 'FREE LUNCH TODAY! Scan to claim your voucher.'

inspect.c: The code is a sticker, stuck slightly crooked on top of the printed poster.
No team name or contact. Cafeteria notices come from Facilities.
Your camera preview shows nova-lunch-voucher.click/login. That's not a novacorp.com address.

acts.l: Scan it and sign in to claim lunch
acts.fb: The page was a fake sign-in. Your password now belongs to someone else.

acts.l: Report the poster to IT
acts.fb: IT and Facilities can take it down before others scan it.

acts.l: Ignore it
acts.fb: You're safe, but colleagues may still fall for it.

enc.lesson: A QR code is just a link you can't read. Treat it like any other link.

enc.title: A sticky note on a monitor

art.desc: On a colleague's monitor: a yellow note reading 'VPN: Summer2026!'. The desk is empty.

inspect.c: It's a live VPN password, visible to anyone walking past.
The computer isn't locked either.

acts.l: Tell the owner and IT so the password gets changed
acts.fb: Exposed passwords need changing, not just hiding.

acts.l: Leave it, it's not your desk
acts.fb: Not your fault, but the password stays exposed.

acts.l: Try it to see if it still works
acts.fb: Using someone else's credentials is a breach in itself.

acts.l: Take a photo to remind them later
acts.fb: Now the password is on your phone too.

enc.lesson: Passwords belong in a password manager, never on paper or a screen edge.

enc.title: An unlocked laptop in the meeting room

art.desc: A laptop on the meeting table, unlocked, with the Finance inbox open. The meeting ended twenty minutes ago.

inspect.c: The Finance inbox is open. Anyone could read or send email as its owner.
Empty. People walk past the glass wall all the time.

acts.l: Lock the screen (Windows + L) and tell the owner
acts.fb: Two seconds, and nobody can use that session.

acts.l: Close the lid and leave it
acts.fb: Some laptops don't lock on close. Locking is safer.

acts.l: Read the emails to find out whose it is
acts.fb: That's reading confidential data you have no right to see.

acts.l: Carry it to IT
acts.fb: Well meant, but locking it and telling the owner is quicker and safer.

enc.lesson: Lock your screen every time you stand up: Windows + L, or Ctrl + Cmd + Q on a Mac.

levels.title: Inbox Defense
levels.blurb: Six messages need your decision. Spot lookalike domains, fake logins and poisoned attachments, and trust the real ones.
intro: Monday, 10:05 AM. Your inbox has filled up overnight.
Process each email at your desk. Inspect before you decide: check the sender, hover over links, look at attachments.
Some of these are real. Reporting a genuine email costs time too.

enc.title: Action required: your password expires in 24 hours

art.subj: Action required: your password expires in 24 hours
body: Your NovaCorp password will expire in 24 hours. To keep your current password and avoid losing access to email and files, confirm it now.
If you do not act, your account will be locked.

inspect.c: novac0rp-support.com has a zero instead of an 'o', and it isn't novacorp.com.
It goes to novac0rp-support.com, not the company intranet.
A 24-hour deadline and a threat of being locked out. Pressure is the oldest trick.

acts.l: Click the link and sign in
acts.fb: You just typed your password into an attacker's page.

acts.l: Report it with the Report Phish button
acts.fb: Reported. IT can now block it for everyone.

acts.l: Delete it
acts.fb: You're safe, but reporting protects colleagues too.

acts.l: Reply and ask if it is real
acts.fb: The attacker reads replies and will say yes. Check through a channel you trust.

enc.lesson: IT never asks you to confirm a password through an email link. Go to the intranet yourself.

enc.title: Priya shared 'Q4 Salary Revisions.xlsx' with you

art.subj: Priya shared 'Q4 Salary Revisions.xlsx' with you
body: Priya Sharma has shared a file with you.
Q4 Salary Revisions.xlsx: 'Please review before Friday. Keep this confidential.'

inspect.c: novadrive-share.co isn't NovaCorp's file service. Real shares come from drive.novacorp.com.
It opens a sign-in page on novadrive-share.co.
Why would HR send salary data to a new intern? The juicy title is the bait.

acts.l: Open it and sign in to view
acts.fb: A fake sign-in page just captured your credentials.

acts.l: Report it
acts.fb: Right call. IT will warn anyone else who received it.

acts.l: Ask Priya on NovaChat if she sent it
acts.fb: Checking through a separate, trusted channel is exactly right.

acts.l: Ignore it
acts.fb: Safe for you, but a report would protect others.

enc.lesson: Unexpected 'shared file' emails are a favourite phishing format. Check the domain before you sign in anywhere.

enc.title: Planned maintenance Saturday 10 PM

body: The VPN and email will be offline this Saturday from 10 PM to midnight for upgrades.
No action is needed. Please save your work before you log off on Friday.

inspect.c: dev@novacorp.com matches the IT Helpdesk entry in the company directory.
None. It asks you for nothing.
No pressure and no request for passwords. It's purely informational.

acts.l: Note it and carry on
acts.fb: Correct. This one is genuine.

acts.l: Report it as phishing
acts.fb: This one was real. Over-reporting costs IT time, so check the sender and the request first.

acts.l: Forward it to your whole team
acts.fb: Harmless, but it already went to everyone.

enc.lesson: Not every email is a threat. A known sender, no links and no request for credentials is a good sign.

enc.title: OVERDUE: Invoice #4471 payment failed

body: Our records show invoice #4471 is overdue. Please open the attached invoice and confirm your payment details today to avoid late fees.

inspect.c: acme-supp1ies.com uses the number 1 instead of the letter l.
An .html file posing as an invoice. Opening it shows a fake login page.
You're an intern. You don't handle vendor invoices, and NovaCorp doesn't use Acme.

acts.l: Open the invoice
acts.fb: The 'invoice' was a credential-harvesting page.

acts.l: Report it
acts.fb: Good. Invoice lures are one of the most common phishing types.

acts.l: Forward it to Finance to deal with
acts.fb: You've just sent the trap to the people with payment access.

acts.l: Delete it
acts.fb: Safe, but reporting helps IT block the sender.

enc.lesson: Invoices arrive as PDFs from known vendors. An .html attachment is a red flag on its own.

enc.title: Welcome to NovaCorp! Your onboarding checklist

art.subj: Welcome to NovaCorp! Your onboarding checklist
body: Your onboarding checklist is on the HR portal. Please complete it by the end of your first week.

inspect.c: priya@novacorp.com, the real HR address.
hr.novacorp.com/onboarding: the company's own HR portal.
No threats, a reasonable deadline, and it matches what Mira told you.

acts.l: Open the HR portal
acts.fb: Correct. Genuine email, genuine portal.

acts.l: Report it as phishing
acts.fb: This was legitimate. Being too suspicious slows everyone down.

acts.l: Ignore it
acts.fb: No risk, but you'd miss your onboarding tasks.

enc.lesson: Verify, then act. When the sender, link and request all check out, it's fine to proceed.

enc.title: Rex wants you to open an attachment

lines: Hey! Can you open this attachment for me? It's a contract from some vendor.
It won't open on my laptop. Something about 'enable macros'. Maybe yours will work?

inspect.c: 'Some vendor,' says Rex. 'Never heard of them, but the subject says URGENT.'
Contract_Final.docm: a macro-enabled Word document.

acts.l: Open it on your laptop and enable macros
acts.fb: Macros in unexpected documents are a classic way to install malware.

acts.l: Tell Rex not to enable macros and to report it
acts.fb: Rex grumbles, but he reports it. Crisis avoided.

acts.l: Say you're busy
acts.fb: Rex will just ask someone else.

enc.lesson: Never enable macros in a document you weren't expecting.

levels.title: Calls & Messages
levels.blurb: Vishing calls, smishing texts, MFA-fatigue attacks and a fake CFO on WhatsApp. One request is genuine.
intro: Tuesday. Attackers know email filters are getting better, so today they'll call and text instead.
Your desk phone and your mobile will light up around the office. Each one is marked in gold.
Remember: a caller ID or a profile picture proves nothing.

enc.title: Incoming call from "IT Support"

lines: Hi, this is Arun from NovaCorp IT. We're seeing suspicious sign-ins on your account.
I'm sending a code to your phone. Read it back to me and I'll lock the attacker out.
Quickly please, they're still logged in!

inspect.c: An external number, not the internal helpdesk on extension 4357.
'There's no time for a ticket!' He dodges the question.
A one-time code proves you are you. Anyone asking for it wants to log in as you.

acts.l: Read the code out to him
acts.fb: He just used your code to sign in to your account.

acts.l: Hang up and call the helpdesk on 4357
acts.fb: Dev confirms nobody from IT called you. Reported.

acts.l: Ask him to email you instead
acts.fb: He'll just send a phishing email. Calling the helpdesk yourself is safest.

enc.lesson: Never share a one-time code. Not with IT, not with your bank, not with anyone.

enc.title: A text about a parcel

art.text: NovaPost: your parcel is on hold due to an unpaid customs fee of ₹49. Pay within 12 hrs or it will be returned:

inspect.c: A random mobile number, not a courier's short code.
novapost-delivery.top: a cheap domain unrelated to any real courier.
Are you even expecting a parcel? Tiny fees and tight deadlines are classic bait.

acts.l: Pay the ₹49
acts.fb: Your card details are now with scammers, and the fee was never the point.

acts.l: Delete it and report it as spam
acts.fb: Good. Reporting helps carriers block the number.

acts.l: Reply STOP
acts.fb: Replying confirms your number is active.

enc.lesson: Couriers don't ask for fees by text link. Track parcels in the official app.

enc.title: Five sign-in requests in two minutes

inspect.c: Moscow. You're sitting in the Bengaluru office.
No. You haven't tried to sign in anywhere.
Five prompts in two minutes. Someone is trying to wear you down.

acts.l: Approve one to make them stop
acts.fb: That approval let the attacker straight in. They already had your password.

acts.l: Deny, report to IT and change your password
acts.fb: Exactly. The prompts mean your password is already out there.

acts.l: Ignore them
acts.fb: Not approving is good, but IT needs to know your password leaked.

enc.lesson: An MFA prompt you didn't start means someone has your password. Deny it and report it.

enc.title: Dev asks you to restart your laptop

lines: Hey, about your ticket #4471, the slow laptop.
I've pushed an update. Can you restart now? I'll watch it come back online from my side.

inspect.c: Ticket #4471 is yours. You raised it this morning.
It's Dev, in person, at the helpdesk.
Just a restart. No passwords, no codes.

acts.l: Restart the laptop
acts.fb: Correct. A verified request that asks for nothing sensitive.

acts.l: Refuse and report Dev to Security
acts.fb: Dev is the real helpdesk, working on your own ticket.

acts.l: Ask him to email the request first
acts.fb: Not wrong, but it was already verified in person.

enc.lesson: Trust is fine when you've verified who is asking and what they want.

enc.title: WhatsApp from a new number

msgs: Hi, this is Hale. New number, my old phone broke.
I need a favour. Buy 5 Amazon gift cards of ₹10,000 for a client and send me the codes. I'll reimburse you today.
Keep this between us. It's very urgent.

inspect.c: It isn't in your contacts, and it isn't Hale's number in the directory.
Gift cards, secrecy and urgency together: the classic CEO-fraud recipe.
Real expenses go through the finance portal, never your personal card.

acts.l: Buy the gift cards
acts.fb: ₹50,000 gone. Gift card codes are as good as cash.

acts.l: Verify with Mr. Hale through a known channel
acts.fb: Hale is in his office and has no idea what you're talking about.

acts.l: Ignore it
acts.fb: Safe for you, but Security should know someone is impersonating the CFO.

acts.l: Reply asking who it really is
acts.fb: The scammer will just insist it's Hale.

enc.lesson: A new number plus urgency plus secrecy is a scam until proven otherwise.

levels.title: Access Control
levels.blurb: Doors, badges and confident strangers. Decide who gets in, what gets shared and who simply needs directions.
intro: Wednesday. Today the attackers come in person.
People with boxes, uniforms and confident stories. Some are exactly who they say they are.
Ask, verify, and when in doubt, send them to reception.

enc.title: A courier asks you to badge him in

lines: Morning! Big delivery for the third floor.
My hands are full. Could you tap your badge on the side door and hold it for me? Reception is so slow.

inspect.c: No visitor badge or sign-in sticker.
The boxes have no NovaCorp label or delivery slip.
He's asking you to bypass reception, the one checkpoint for visitors.

acts.l: Badge him in and hold the door
acts.fb: Whoever he really is, he's now inside with no record of entry.

acts.l: Point him to reception to sign in
acts.fb: Polite and firm. Reception handles every visitor.

acts.l: Walk away without a word
acts.fb: He'll try the next person. Reception should know.

enc.lesson: Never let anyone follow you through a secure door. Visitors sign in at reception.

enc.title: A contractor wants the server room

lines: Hi, I'm from CoolAir. Here to service the server-room AC.
Ada said it's fine, she's just busy. Can you let me in?

inspect.c: He has no ticket number and 'forgot' the paperwork.
A laminated card with no photo and a logo you don't recognise.
Ada is right inside. Checking takes thirty seconds.

acts.l: Let him into the server room
acts.fb: Physical access to servers is the jackpot for an attacker.

acts.l: Ask him to wait while you check with Ada
acts.fb: Ada has no AC service booked. Security escorts him out.

acts.l: Tell him to come back tomorrow
acts.fb: He'll come back with a better story. Report it today.

enc.lesson: Name-dropping is not authorisation. Verify with the person named.

enc.title: A new hire asks for help

lines: Hi! I'm Kabir, I start in Finance today.
Mira signed me in and gave me my badge. Could you point me to the HR room for my induction?

inspect.c: A proper NovaCorp badge with his photo and today's date.
Mira nods: 'Yes, Kabir's on my list. Welcome!'
Directions to HR. No access to anything sensitive.

acts.l: Show him the way to HR
acts.fb: A verified colleague, a harmless request. Being helpful is part of security culture.

acts.l: Call Security on him
acts.fb: He was signed in and badged. That's a wasted call.

acts.l: Refuse to help
acts.fb: Being unhelpful to a verified colleague isn't security.

enc.lesson: Security isn't suspicion of everyone. Verify, then help.

enc.title: A confidential printout left in the tray

art.desc: A stack of pages titled 'Q3 salary bands: CONFIDENTIAL'. Nobody has collected it for an hour.

inspect.c: Salary data for every team.
Printed by Priya in HR, an hour ago.
The printer sits in a busy corridor next to the water cooler.

acts.l: Take it straight to Priya in HR
acts.fb: Priya thanks you and switches to secure print.

acts.l: Leave it there
acts.fb: Anyone could pick it up.

acts.l: Read through it
acts.fb: You've just seen everyone's salary. That's a data leak in itself.

acts.l: Throw it in the bin
acts.fb: Bins aren't shredders. People do go through office rubbish.

enc.lesson: Use secure print, collect printouts straight away, and shred what you don't need.

enc.title: A visitor asks network questions

lines: Hi! I'm Zoe from NetSecure, doing a quick network audit for your IT team.
What's the office WiFi password, and which VPN app do you use? Just ticking boxes.

inspect.c: A visitor badge, but it says 'Catering'.
No audit is on the IT calendar today.
WiFi passwords and VPN details help an attacker get inside the network.

acts.l: Share the details, it sounds official
acts.fb: Pretexting works because it sounds routine.

acts.l: Say you can't share that, and alert IT
acts.fb: IT has never heard of NetSecure. Good catch.

acts.l: Send her to reception for the guest WiFi
acts.fb: Better than sharing, but the fake audit should be reported.

enc.lesson: Real auditors go through IT, never through random employees in the cafeteria.

levels.title: Executive Floor
levels.blurb: The boss level. A multi-stage CEO fraud through email, chat and a cloned voice, plus a vendor bank switch and one genuine payment.
intro: Friday. You're covering for Mr. Hale's assistant on the executive floor.
Someone is about to try to move ₹18.5 lakh out of the company. It will look like it comes from the very top.
The CEO fraud happens in stages. Each stage unlocks the next.

tasks.label: Stage 1: urgent email from the CEO

enc.title: Confidential: urgent wire before 4 PM

body: We're closing a confidential acquisition today. I need you to wire ₹18,50,000 to our new legal partner before 4 PM.
Account: 50200081472219 · IFSC: HDFC0004471 · Larkspur Legal LLP
Do not discuss this with anyone, including Finance. I'm in meetings all day, so email only.

inspect.c: novacorp-exec.com is not novacorp.com. Anyone can register a lookalike domain.
Secrecy, a hard deadline and 'don't tell Finance'. Every pressure lever at once.
Payments over ₹1 lakh need CFO approval in the finance portal. This skips it.

acts.l: Send the wire
acts.fb: ₹18.5 lakh is gone, and banks rarely recover BEC losses.

acts.l: Verify with Mr. Hale in the finance portal
acts.fb: There is no such request in the portal. You've stopped stage one.

acts.l: Reply and ask if it is really her
acts.fb: The attacker controls that inbox and will say yes.

acts.l: Forward it to Finance to pay
acts.fb: You've passed the fraud to the people who can actually send money.

enc.lesson: Any payment request that bypasses the normal approval process is a red flag, whoever it claims to come from.

enc.title: NovaChat message from "Elena Vance"

msgs: Did you see my email? This can't wait.
The board is watching this deal. I'll remember who helped today.
Just send it, then send me the receipt.

inspect.c: 'External': this account is outside the NovaCorp workspace.
Flattery plus pressure: 'I'll remember who helped today.'
Elena's calendar shows her on a flight right now.

acts.l: Send the wire to make the pressure stop
acts.fb: Pressure is the attacker's main tool. It worked.

acts.l: Report the account to IT Security
acts.fb: IT blocks the external account and alerts the leadership team.

acts.l: Mute the chat
acts.fb: You resisted, but Security needs to know.

enc.lesson: Attackers switch channels to add pressure. A second channel is not a second proof.

enc.title: Conference phone: "Elena Vance"

lines: It's Elena. I'm about to board. Listen, the wire has to go now.
I know it's unusual. I'm authorising it personally. Do it and I'll sort out the paperwork later.

inspect.c: A UK number. Elena's mobile is in the directory, and it isn't this one.
The voice sounds slightly flat, with odd pauses. Voices can be cloned from public videos.
You ask about this morning's all-hands. 'No time for this!' She dodges.

acts.l: Send the wire, she authorised it
acts.fb: A cloned voice is still a fraud. The money is gone.

acts.l: Hang up and call Elena's directory number
acts.fb: The real Elena is boarding a plane, horrified. You stopped all three stages.

acts.l: Tell her you'll do it after lunch
acts.fb: You bought time, but you should hang up and verify now.

enc.lesson: Hang up and call back on a number you already trust. Voices and faces can be faked.

enc.title: Mr. Hale asks you to check a payment

lines: Ah, good, you're here.
I've raised payment request FIN-2291 for our cleaning vendor in the finance portal. It's approved on my side.
Could you mark it as checked? Same vendor as every month.

inspect.c: FIN-2291 is in the finance portal with Hale's approval attached.
BrightClean, paid monthly for two years, to the same bank account as always.
Mr. Hale, in person, using the normal process.

acts.l: Mark it as checked in the portal
acts.fb: Correct. Right person, right process, known vendor.

acts.l: Refuse and report it as fraud
acts.fb: This was the proper process. Not everything urgent is fraud.

acts.l: Ask him to email you first
acts.fb: Harmless, but he's already using the proper channel.

enc.lesson: Real requests follow the process. That's what makes fakes easy to spot.

enc.title: Updated bank details for future payments

art.subj: Updated bank details for future payments
body: Due to an audit, our bank account has changed. Please update our details before your next payment run.
Kindly confirm once updated. Regards, Ramesh

inspect.c: brightclean-services.in, but BrightClean always writes from brightclean.in.
It changes where money goes, right before a payment run.
Vendor bank changes must be confirmed by phone, on the number in the contract.

acts.l: Update the bank details
acts.fb: Next month's payment goes straight to the attacker.

acts.l: Call BrightClean on the number in the contract
acts.fb: BrightClean's bank details haven't changed. Fraud stopped.

acts.l: Reply to the email to confirm
acts.fb: Replying reaches the attacker, who will happily confirm.

acts.l: Forward it to Finance to check
acts.fb: Better than acting on it, but you could have verified it yourself.

enc.lesson: Always confirm bank-detail changes by phone, using contact details you already had.
